explain.say: Stations are told apart by frequency, how many waves pass each second. An FM station sends about 100 million waves a second, each about 3 metres long.

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Each station has its own frequency

faq.q: What does a radio transmitter do?
faq.a: It makes a fast electrical wobble called a carrier wave, at the station's frequency, and changes it in step with the sound from the microphone. That combined signal is sent to the mast.

faq.q: How does the mast send out radio waves?
faq.a: The transmitter makes electrons in the mast surge up and down millions of times a second. Charges moving like this send out radio waves, which spread out at the speed of light.

faq.q: How does an aerial pick up radio waves?
faq.a: When radio waves pass a metal aerial, they push its electrons back and forth, making tiny currents. Every station's waves do this at once, each at its own frequency.

faq.q: How does a radio pick one station out of many?
faq.a: The tuner is a circuit that resonates at just one frequency, like a swing pushed in time. Turning the dial changes that frequency, so only the chosen station's signal is boosted.
asks: What does tuning a radio do?

faq.q: How does the radio turn the signal back into sound?
faq.a: The radio strips away the carrier wave and keeps the sound pattern, then amplifies it and sends it to a speaker, which moves the air just as the microphone was moved.
asks: How does a radio make sound?

facts: Radio waves travel at the speed of light, about 300,000 kilometres per second.
Guglielmo Marconi sent the first radio signal across the Atlantic in 1901.

quiz.say: What does the tuner in a radio do?
quiz.show: What does the tuner in a radio do?
quiz.why: The aerial collects every station at once; the tuner resonates at one frequency so only that station gets through.

wrong.1: Radio waves are made by the transmitter and mast, not your radio.
wrong.2: That is the transmitter's job at the studio.
